## Headline findings

**1. Does the best T04 variant beat T03 on R@10 per stem?** Four out of five
yes, one no.

| Stem | T03 R@10 | best T04 R@10 (variant) | Δ | T04 wins? |
|---|---:|---|---:|:---:|
| doc 5 — Code Jud. (S) | 0.3910 | 0.4678 (`node_raw / enriched / node_full`) | +0.077 | yes |
| doc 6 — Code Pénal    | 0.2985 | 0.2474 (`article_raw / article_full`) | -0.051 | **no** |
| doc 9 — Code Civil    | 0.4713 | 0.5137 (`node_summary`) | +0.042 | yes |
| doc 8 — Loi (rentals) | 0.8006 | 0.8045 (`node_summary`) | +0.004 | yes (thin) |
| doc 7 — Code Jud. (L) | 0.3425 | 0.3461 (`node_summary`) | +0.004 | yes (thin) |

**Doc 6 flip:** *No.* Doc 6 remains the lone stem where T03 wins R@10 even
under linker v4 — the gap (Δ = -0.051) is similar to the v3 sweep (T03 0.330
vs T04 0.274, Δ = -0.056). The v4 linker fix did not move doc 6's verdict;
the deficit is a true T04 weakness on this PDF and is the right place to drill
into in §3a if you run the optional analysis.

**2. Which T04 variant is best overall?** `arm2_metadata_node_summary`,
mean rank 2.591 across 22 (stem × metric) cells — comfortably ahead of the
runners-up (article_raw / article_full tied at 2.773; the three node_raw /
enriched / full clones tied at 2.955 because they collapse to identical
numbers on the recall-style metrics). This confirms v3's finding that node-
level chunking with LLM-generated summary text is the strongest T04 variant.

**3. Pool breadth vs precision tradeoff.** T03 still wins R@100 on **4/5
stems** (doc 5, 9, 8, 7); only doc 6 flips, where `node_summary` lifts R@100
from 0.640 to 0.706. So the broad pattern from v3 holds: T03's naive hybrid
casts a wider but less precise net, T04 (especially `node_summary`) gives up
some breadth in exchange for substantially better top-10 precision (MRR@10
+0.10 mean, nDCG@10 +0.08 mean; T04 wins MRR@10 and nDCG@10 on 5/5 stems).

**4. Cosine-weighted metrics.** Only doc 9 carries `Cw/R@10` / `Cw/R@100`
(T07 cosine GT not available for the other four subsets, as predicted from
the v3 sweep). On doc 9 the cosine-weighted metrics mirror the binary
direction: at K=10 `node_summary` beats T03 (0.515 vs 0.469); at K=100 T03
still wins (0.929 vs 0.872). No verdict flips from binary → cosine on the one
stem where both exist.
